name: GEF Small Grants Programme Sri Lanka

administered_by.name: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)

summary: Sri Lanka's GEF Small Grants component run by IUCN with CEPF, giving grants of up to US$60,000 to local civil society groups for community engagement in managing threatened ecosystems and species in five districts.

geography.label: Nuwara Eliya, Kegalle, Ratnapura, Galle and Matara districts

eligibility.rule: Legally registered in Sri Lanka and eligible to receive foreign contributions
Project is located in one or more of the five eligible districts
Restoration, habitat improvement or management activities are outside Protected Areas
No land purchase, cultural property removal, resettlement or trust fund capitalisation
Project supports community engagement in managing threatened species and ecosystems

administered_by.quote: The Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF) and IUCN, International Union for Conservation of Nature, are currently accepting Letters of Inquiry (LOIs) from Sri Lankan non-governmental organizations, community-based organizations, Indigenous People's organizations,

applicant_types.quote: from Sri Lankan non-governmental organizations, community-based organizations, Indigenous People's organizations, women's groups, youth groups and other civil society organizations

geography.quote: Eligible districts: Nuwara Eliya, Kegalle, Ratnapura, Galle and Matara

access.quote: are currently accepting Letters of Inquiry (LOIs) from Sri Lankan non-governmental organizations

window.quote: Sign up for the CEPF newsletter to receive announcements for future calls for proposals

effort.quote: Call for Letters of Inquiry, GEF Small Grants Program, Sri Lanka - CI/CEPF and IUCN Eligible Country: Sri Lanka Opening Date: Wednesday, 9 September 2026 Closing Date: Friday, 9 October 2026
All LOIs submitted will first be screened to confirm their eligibility. Eligible LOIs will then undergo preliminary reviews utilising the criteria mentioned above.
Based on these reviews, shortlisted applications will be further considered during a meeting of the National Steering Committee (NSC) joined by the Ministry of Environment.
Following the recommendations of the NSC, organizations whose LOIs are selected will be invited to submit full project proposals.

eligibility.quote: Please note that this call is restricted to applications from Sri Lankan organizations that are legally registered and eligible to receive foreign contributions.
Projects must be located within one or more of the following five districts to be eligible for this call: Nuwara Eliya; Kegalle; Ratnapura; Galle; and Matara.
Therefore, restoration, habitat improvement, or other management activities within Protected Areas are not eligible for funding under this call.

Grants cannot be used for: (i) purchase of land; (ii) removal or alteration of any physical cultural property (including those with archaeological, palaeontological, historical, religious or unique natural values); (iii) relocation of people or any other form of involuntary resettlement; or (iv) capitalization of trust funds.
Projects must support community engagement in management of threatened ecosystems and species within eligible districts in central and southwestern Sri Lanka.

documents.quote: Applicants should submit a copy of their legal registration together with their LOI.
